div.head: A database of early English lawcodes
div.p: The eLiebermann Lawcodes Database brings together and makes searchable the law codes of early England. The core of the database consists of the Old English or Latin text, as printed in Felix Liebermann's Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, with Liebermann's German translation and a literal English rendering of his German. To allow for quick comparison, additional MS variants, editions and alternate translations are provided where available.

Every clause is further indexed by subject, so the laws can be searched by the people, offences, places and topics they deal with. Cross-references collate possible connections to clauses in other codes, gathering the suggestions of a range of scholars and editors. Liebermann's editorial notes will be added as the database grows.

div.head: A dictionary of early English law
div.p: The eLiebermann Legal Dictionary is a digital edition of the Wörterbuch, the dictionary in Volume II of Felix Liebermann's Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen. Liebermann's dictionary covers the Old English, Latin and French words of the law codes he edited. This digital version provides links to explanations and translations of Liebermann's grammatical terms, abbreviations, and sigla, and to the law-code clauses (in the Laws Database) that Liebermann lists as containing the headword.

div.head: A guide to Liebermann's Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen
div.p: The eLiebermann Guide to the Gesetze aims to make Felix Liebermann's Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen easier to use. Liebermann's academic German makes heavy use of abbreviation, and his apparatus is dense. The guides expand and translate all three, and every technical term or abbreviation in the dictionary is linked to a translation.

The Guide to the Gesetze also gives Liebermann's own account of how to read a dictionary entry, translated into English, with a key to his system for citing the laws; and it contains Liebermann's list of the manuscripts in which the laws survive, with their dates and contents (as Liebermann explains them). As the database grows, additional or corrective information will be added to this portion of the database.
